content.thinking:
I'm planning the biplane's proportions and dimensions, with a whimsical chunky style in cheerful red, yellow, and cream tones, making sure it's oriented correctly and sits properly on its wheels.

Now I'm sketching out the skeleton structure with a root fuselage joint and hinges for the propeller, wheels, rudder, elevators, and ailerons, keeping the joint count minimal and being careful about API pitfalls like unused imports. I'm working out how to orient cylindrical parts like the propeller using direction vectors, and starting to define the fuselage as a loft shape tapering from a rounded nose cowl at the front to a narrower tail.

Writing the paint function for the cel-shaded cream body with a red stripe band...

Now I'm sketching the cowl as a lathed ring shape with outer/inner wall points, plus a dark recessed disc and seven small cylinder shapes to suggest radial engine cylinders around the front. I'm shifting focus to the upper wing placement next, setting its height, span, and chord dimensions.

Still refining paint logic...

Setting the lower wing at y=1.0, span 6.6, chord 1.15, centered at z=0.75, letting it pass through the fuselage body near its bottom which matches the low-wing reference. Upper wing sits at 2.55 giving a 1.55m gap, with the pilot cockpit positioned behind at z≈-0.5, consistent with the reference layout.

For the ailerons, I'll skip real hinge extrusions and instead add cosmetic red-tipped plates near the trailing edge of the upper wing, with hinge joints placed symmetrically along the x-axis. For the interplane struts, I'm planning two N-strut pairs per side connecting the lower wing at y=1.0 to the upper wing at y=2.5, positioned near the front and rear of the wing span, colored wooden-orange to match the reference biplane look.

Now I'm adding cabane struts between the fuselage top and the upper wing center, plus thin diagonal bracing wires crossing between the strut endpoints for visual authenticity, using small radius rods with dark grey coloring and flat caps to avoid degenerate geometry. I'm being careful to specify bone assignments explicitly near areas like the wheels where joint proximity could cause ambiguity.

I'm setting up the landing gear with V-struts running from the fuselage bottom to the axle, a horizontal cross tube connecting the wheel hubs, and cylindrical wheels sized so their tires rest on the ground plane.

For the wheels themselves, I'm orienting the hub and tire geometry correctly along the x-axis using torus shapes for rounder tires, adding hub discs with cream caps, and keeping everything low-poly with flat shading.

Now I'm working out the landing gear struts connecting the fuselage to the wheels, plus the axle rod between them. For the tail, I'm sketching out the fin and rudder as 2D outline shapes extruded with thickness, positioning the fixed fin near the back of the fuselage and giving the rudder its own hinge joint so it can rotate, working through the coordinate math to get the outline points and hinge axis oriented correctly.

Still refining the tail shapes... I'm adjusting the rudder polygon points so they close properly without edge crossings, then fitting the fixed fin in front of it so the trailing edge height matches the rudder's leading edge. I'm also checking the fuselage taper near the tail tip and starting to think through the horizontal stabilizer as another extruded plan shape.

Working out the elevator extrusion geometry, extending from the hinge line rearward along z with a tapered outline, and placing the hinge joints along the x-axis.

Now I'm designing the pilot: a cream-skinned sphere head wearing a brown leather helmet with blue cylindrical goggle lenses and a trailing white scarf, seated in a cockpit opening lined with a flat torus coaming ring, red jacket peeking out, plus a small tilted windscreen plane.

Adding the scarf sweep with a tapered box section following curved points, then designing a wooden two-blade propeller attached at the fuselage nose.

Still shaping propeller geometry...

Now I'm checking the fuselage station profile, defining width and height at each z-position from tail to nose to shape the body contour.

Writing the stripe coloring logic...

Still working through the paint and geometry logic, confirming the lit/shadow resolution works, then moving to the wing colors and panel lines before placing the engine cylinders radially around the cowl opening with dark steel coloring.

Writing paint zigzag logic...

Adding small exhaust rods on the fuselage sides near the nose, then working out a flattened headrest hump behind the pilot and checking fuselage height at that point.

Now I'm figuring out the cockpit ring geometry, trying to get a torus oriented and scaled correctly to sit flat with a stretched profile given the axis alignment constraints.

Simplifying, I settle on a uniform circular ring instead, with a dark leather-brown disc cylinder seat at its center. Then I move to the pilot figure: positioning a skin-toned head and red shoulders above the coaming, with a brown helmet piece to add on top.

Adding more geometry details...

Now I'm figuring out the tail skid position, placing a small post running from the fuselage bottom near the tail down to around y 0.12, keeping it short enough to look proportional for a biplane at rest.

I'm then checking that the wheels actually touch the ground plane at y=0, adjusting the axle heights and torus radii so the tire bottoms sit flush rather than floating or clipping, and doing the same for the tail wheel. Finally I'm confirming the overall aircraft height stays reasonable with the fin and upper wing stacked on top, and double-checking that wheel joints are positioned correctly along the x-axis.

Now I'm setting up the root fuselage joint and building helper functions for creating parts attached to the fuselage bone, plus picking a small flat color palette for the paint scheme.

Writing wing rib paint function...

Adding a gold rim band between the red and yellow regions, then setting up the wing extrusion with positioning, thickness, bevel, and smoothing parameters for the rounded rectangular shape.

Checking that the corner-rounding smoothing won't overlap at these dimensions, but realizing a plain rounded rectangle would taper the wingtips too aggressively into an elliptical shape. I'm switching to building a custom wing outline function with explicit arc points at the tips for better control over the tip curvature...

Still writing wing outline points...

Working out the aileron geometry now, trying to position a trailing box piece behind the wing rim and settle on its color so it doesn't clash with the red outline already there.

I'm also thinking about adding roundel numbers as decals on the fuselage and wing underside, but the fuselage width varies along the z-axis so placing a flat decal plane at a given x offset is tricky to get aligned correctly.

Switching to simpler roundels: using a star emblem (symmetric, so mirroring left/right is no issue) in red/yellow/cream, plus tail rudder stripes, and placing a plane decal on the wing's upper surface slightly above the wing's actual top height so it doesn't clip.

Mirroring the roundel on the underside and opposite wing works cleanly since the design is symmetric, and I'm using transparent PNG/SVG corners so only the circular emblem shows. Writing the SVG for the roundel now...

For struts, I'll keep them a plain wood color rather than textured grain to save atlas space, add small steel fitting boxes at the joints, and figure out strut placement/count per side using N-strut spacing along the fuselage.

Placing struts vertically at staggered x positions between the lower and upper wing anchor points, with front and rear pairs on each side totaling 8 struts, then adding diagonal wire connections between adjacent strut rows for rigidity.

Still defining strut geometry...

Thinking about whimsical extras like a small pennant flag on the upper wing strut, made from a pole rod and a triangular flag shape, but deciding to keep most add-ons minimal.

Instead of trying to scatter rivets across the fuselage surface which feels too risky to compute, I'll skip full rivet detailing and just place a ring of small spheres around the cowl rim for a simple riveted look.

I'm checking the rod function signature and part options like bone binding and sides, confirming the lathe orientation with axis and outline conventions, then setting up the fuselage sweep using loft with station arrays and a paint-based color fallback.

Writing fuselage paint logic...

Checking the cowl-to-fuselage joint and wheel placement, then defining the prop blade coloring and wheel assembly—tire, hub, cap, and axle parts with their positions and colors.

Setting up the leg struts connecting fuselage to wheels, plus the tail wheel assembly with its small torus tire and support strut, then moving to pilot details and fin stripe coloring based on position.

Writing paint pattern logic...

Now I'm placing the stabilizer and elevator, checking that their positions along z don't overlap badly and working out the elevator's hinge joint and outline coordinates relative to the stab.

I'm then figuring out the rudder hinge placement, its fin geometry, and verifying the fin base sits just under the fuselage top at the tail so the attachment looks clean.

For the propeller blades, I'm setting up two blade extrusions mounted at the hub with opposite orientations so they form a symmetric pair spinning around the shaft, sized so the overall prop radius comes to about 1.25.

I'm checking ground clearance and it's fine, and now plotting the scarf curve as a sequence of points trailing back behind the pilot, adjusting the headrest position so it doesn't collide with the scarf's path. I still need to write the Roundel star by computing its points programmatically.
